question: Should OpenClaw accept persisted byte-compaction retry metadata and the 1 MiB/10% material-growth hysteresis as the supported retry policy for byte-triggered preflight compaction?
rationale: The code appears mechanically sound, but the exact retry window and persisted session metadata define user-visible session-state behavior that automation should not choose for maintainers.

options.title: Accept Retry Hysteresis
options.body: Land the PR with the current persisted retry metadata and growth threshold if preventing every-turn byte compaction loops is worth delaying same-transcript byte retries.

options.title: Tune Threshold First
options.body: Change the absolute or relative growth threshold and update the focused regression tests before merging if owners want a different retry policy.

options.title: Pause For Broader Compaction Policy
options.body: Hold this PR if owners want to resolve it together with the adjacent auto-compaction semantics and stale-usage estimator work.

recommendation.title: Accept Retry Hysteresis
recommendation.body: Land the PR with the current persisted retry metadata and growth threshold if preventing every-turn byte compaction loops is worth delaying same-transcript byte retries.
